decisions.title: Release shape
decisions.context: The constitution and #200 require Product and Lab to release together; neither repository has a release yet.
decisions.recommendation: Keep the joint v0.1.0 release. Do not reopen product-only versus joint-release strategy now.

options.label: Joint Product + Lab v0.1.0
options.description: Preserves the governed Product/Lab story and existing owner decision.

options.label: Product-only v0.1.0
options.description: Faster, but supersedes an explicit decision and weakens the research-companion narrative.

options.label: Defer both until #174
options.description: Polishes first, but contradicts the release programme and delays learning.

decisions.title: Open security dependency PR #323
decisions.context: The only open Product PR is a mergeable Dependabot security update with the hosted proving gate green.
decisions.recommendation: Re-run or confirm exact-head CI, inspect the lockfile-only diff, then merge before cutting release artifacts.

options.label: Merge after exact-head recheck
options.description: Closes known high-severity transitive parser advisories before release.

options.label: Hold until release branch
options.description: Avoids a moving base, but ships a known security update later than necessary.

decisions.title: Final Product visual sign-off
decisions.context: Chris0Jeky/developer-lens::HUMAN_TODO.md::q-10(c) is the sole current tag-blocking owner action; Lab visual sign-off is already complete.
decisions.recommendation: Use one bounded proof packet: desktop full page, above fold, 390×844 mobile, 30–60 second scroll video, checksums and exact commit.

options.label: Review and approve bounded packet
options.description: Closes the only release-blocking human gate without reopening design.

options.label: Request one bounded polish pass
options.description: Use only for concrete visible defects; cap at one pass.

options.label: Reopen visual direction
options.description: High delay and scope risk; inappropriate for v0.1 unless the experience is unusable.

decisions.title: Post-release order
decisions.context: #304 has an external consumer and a narrow contract; #174 is the flagship value vertical.
decisions.recommendation: Ship #304 immediately after release, then make #174 the dominant product lane.

options.label: #304 then #174
options.description: Unblocks CommitAtlas quickly and then returns focus to core product value.

options.label: #174 before #304
options.description: Maximizes internal value, but leaves a bounded cross-repo consumer waiting.

options.label: Run both in parallel
options.description: Feasible only with strict file ownership and no shared-contract overlap.

decisions.title: GitHub milestone model
decisions.context: All 52 open issues currently lack milestones, so the GitHub issue list does not convey execution order.
decisions.recommendation: Create four outcome milestones plus a research backlog: v0.1 Release, v0.2 Evidence Flagship, v0.3 Safe Activation, v0.4 Query & Distribution, Research/Later.

options.label: Outcome milestones
options.description: Makes GitHub itself answer what belongs together and why.

options.label: Keep roadmap only in files
options.description: Avoids GitHub administration but keeps portfolio state fragmented.

options.label: Time-boxed sprint milestones
options.description: Simple, but less stable for solo development with uncertain research work.

decisions.title: Governance expansion budget
decisions.context: The repository has a mature governor, prompt OS, context verifier, implementation ledger and friction log. New governance now has diminishing returns.
decisions.recommendation: Freeze new permanent governance mechanisms for two product waves. Allow only fixes that remove a demonstrated repeated failure or replace an older mechanism.

options.label: Two-wave governance freeze
options.description: Redirects effort toward user-visible value while retaining existing safety controls.

options.label: Continue opportunistic governance
options.description: May improve rigor but perpetuates control-plane expansion.

decisions.title: Story-mode identity language
decisions.context: The README still foregrounds Developer DNA, archetypes and rhythms, while the constitution is explicitly system-first and cautious about person scoring.
decisions.recommendation: Keep current language as a clearly labelled personal/legacy Story mode for v0.1; move new surfaces toward Work Shape or System Signature.

options.label: Separate Story and System language
options.description: Preserves charm without contaminating evidence-oriented product claims.

options.label: Keep Developer DNA everywhere
options.description: Memorable, but increasingly clashes with the product's evidentiary posture.

options.label: Remove identity language immediately
options.description: Maximally rigorous, but throws away a distinctive retrospective experience before user learning.
